questions.text: Why does a component declared inside another component lose its state when the parent renders again?
options: The function is new every time. React treats it as a different type and mounts a new instance
An inner component is not allowed to call useState
The parent’s state overwrites the child’s state
This happens only when the inner component has a key

questions.text: What has to match for an instance to keep its state on the next render?
options: Only the variable name that holds the element
The component type and its position in the tree, including key
Only the text the component returned
Only that the parent called the same setter

questions.text: What does changing the key of an already mounted component do?
options: Puts the new key in props and keeps the same state
Only reorders the children and does not touch state
Unmounts the previous instance and mounts a new one with initial state
It is forbidden after the first render

questions.text: Where does a list row’s state go when there is no key and the first item is removed?
options: It moves to the item with the same id
It resets on every remaining row
React refuses to render the list
It stays at the same index. It does not travel with the data

questions.text: When does setState during render not loop the component?
options: When it adjusts state to changed props and sits behind a condition. An unconditional call renders again and again
Always. During render the setter only writes a field
Never. Any setter during render is a syntax error
Only if the component returned null

questions.text: Can you call useState inside an if?
options: Yes. React remembers the hook by the condition text
No. Hooks must run in the same order on every render. A branch breaks that
Yes, if the if comes after the other hooks
Yes, as long as the condition never changes from true to false

questions.text: An effect with [] closed over n, and another effect later called setN. What does the first effect see?
options: The new n, because the effect is still alive
Both values: the old one and the new one
The old n from the render that created it. The empty array does not run it again
undefined. The closure is cleared after setN

questions.text: Does a child lose state if its element is created higher up, passed as children, and a component in between updates its own state?
options: Yes. Any setState higher in the tree remounts the children
Yes, because children is always a new element
Yes, if the child has no key
No. The type and position are the same, so the instance stays

questions.text: Switching the component type in the same position keeps the previous type’s state.
The same type in the same position keeps its state when the parent renders again.
To reset state, the component reads key from the inside as props.key.
key={id} keeps state on the row with the same id, not the same index.
An unconditional setState on every render is a normal way to update the screen.
A hook skipped in one if branch breaks how state lines up between renders.
A lazy useState initializer does not run again when key changes.
The cleanup of an effect with [] runs when the component key changes.
How does React decide that a component instance is the same one?
questions.answer: By the component type and the key at that position in the tree.

questions.text: What happens to state when key changes?
questions.answer: The previous instance unmounts. A new one mounts with initial state.

questions.text: Where does state stick in a list with no key?
questions.answer: To the index. Removing or reordering the data does not take the state with the item.

questions.text: Why does a component function created during render reset state?
questions.answer: Each render produces a new function. React sees a different type and mounts again.

questions.text: When does the cleanup of an effect with an empty dependency array still run?
questions.answer: When the instance unmounts, including when a key change unmounts it.

questions.text: What does an effect with [] see if another effect later updates the variable it closed over?
questions.answer: The value from the render that created this effect. It does not run again.

questions.text: Why does setState during render need a condition?
questions.answer: So state changes only when props changed. A call on every render loops the component.

questions.text: Can you place a hook after an early return?
questions.answer: No. That branch then has fewer hooks, and state lines up wrong.
